doc.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022

title: Innovation as a tricky word: Banff students, Kubrick, Sonny Rollins
summary: Weiss tells of a student at Banff wanting to be an innovator, quotes Kubrick, and argues that perfecting craft matters more and that innovation in swing music is subtle.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: So a lot of it is approach. I wanted to say one thing about the innovation thing. So we were talking about Banff. Wow I got off on a tangent. So I went to Banff I don’t know, right out of college, 1986, 1987. And 25 years later a friend of mine went and Vijay Iyer was the director of the thing. And what sounded like a very Kumbaya moment, I mean you know Banff is in the Canadian Rockies. It’s gorgeous up there. So he had everybody sit outside and introduce themselves, all the students on the first day, introduce themselves and tell what your goals are. Maybe your goals for your career or your goals for the thing.

And my friend told me one kid got up and said, “My name is so-and-so and I want to be an innovator.” And I was like — and he laughed. He was telling me a joke. Like look at these kids, what the? And he’s a kid, he’ll grow up, he’ll figure it out but it’s interesting that some people think that’s how it happens. Or people who are being considered in that realm play with that realm a little bit. You know. It’s an interesting phenomenon. But I mean I’m going to look at it like let’s say Stanley Kubrick. He’s like one of the best filmmakers we ever had. Was he an innovator or did he just do — I think it was a quote of him, I think his quote was everything’s been done, my job is just to do it better than everybody. You know? And that’s — I’m going to keep perfecting my craft whether innovation happens or not it’s not a goal, but I’m going to strive to be the best I can, whatever that means or however that manifests itself. Is somebody going to be an innovator? I don’t know. Will I care? I mean somebody asked me about that a different way, not this way, this way is fun, and I said okay well let me ask you this, if people go to — if an audience goes to a concert tonight are they going to say like I really want to see some great music or are they going to say I want to see some innovation? You know? I mean I hope most people wipe that from their mind. I think certainly there are musicians who know how to manipulate the world they’re living in. They’re clever. They’re smart people and they’re good musicians and they know how to press buttons. I mean I know some guys who are just breaking in, working with a record label like they picked the perfect combination of tunes and musicians that make it pure catnip for the general press. Okay let’s see, let’s do an Andrew Hill tune. Let’s do A Tribe Called Quest tune, let’s you know just push every button. Now you’ve still got to do it well, but there’s a clear path if you think you’re one of those people that are considered in that way. It’d be like okay well let’s continue to press those buttons. Hey! So and it works, but is it innovation? Is it even good? Is it even pure? I mean it’s always good to have goals, it’s always good if you’re going to do a record or a project have a certain thing in your mind about how to go for this, and all the better if you succeed. But you know innovation is a tricky word. I mean I think in more straight ahead realms, more harmony-based swing-

based realms the changes are going to be more subtle and I don’t think people will hear it. I mean a lot of things that are considered innovation these days are more, you’re kind of hitting somebody over the head. The changes have to be bigger for people to recognize them. And I think in the realm of, I think Sonny Rollins spent fifty years perfecting his craft you know. Was he an innovator? I think so at the beginning, but he still kept going. You know? I think it manifests itself in different ways and more subtle ways. And the other thing, if you want to go into the world you’re playing in nobody’s looking for innovation in anything swing-based or harmony based. They put it in a box, it’s been done already, and you know a lot of the music proves them right, but a lot of it doesn’t. And you never hear about it.
